How to Create and Maintain High Powered Teams: It Takes the Power of Influence
abstract: When we think of winning and high performing teams, we think of implementing management tactics, applying techincal and functional knowledge, and following policies and procedures. Building a high performance team requires more than that. Leadership is usually the missing piece when it comes to achieving success and effectiveness at all levels. Leadership is thought of to be as position, titles and strategy but effective leadership involves influence, respect and driving results using non-traditional autocratic methods. In this workshop, we will revisit what true and effective leadership is, and discover the strategies that need to be implemented by technical and engineering professionals to truly create synergy, improved performance and engagement from all levels. A true leadership culture leads to a successful team culture. You will learn the steps to motivate and engage your team for results and learn how to utilize influence strategies to acheive your goals as a team. We will conclude the workshop with a brainstorming session on out of the box ideas that participants can take back to work and begin to implement.

topic: Attracting and Nurturing Talent: Diversity, Inclusion, and Gender Empowerment in Industry
abstract: How do we change to make tomorrow’s workplace welcoming to a diverse, inclusive, gender-empowered one?  Attracting and nurturing talent is essential to the success of a team and to the ultimate success of a company.  How do leaders in industry find, attract and develop talented contributors? Are we doing enough to attract smart, ambitious, energized, new employees? Is there a risk to the status quo if we explicitly make the effort to recruit, hire and develop a truly diverse workforce? We will pose these questions and discuss them.

topic: Developing High Performance Teams in Emerging Non-Traditional Entreprenurial Operations
abstract: Entrepreneurial venture participants are either superstars or oddballs. Both traits are needed. The effort in building a high performing team must focus on finding the mix of innovative off the wall creativity, with the ability to drive fast-paced targets and get things done. Decisions must be made on the fly without all the information, but the aspects of safety and ethics can never be compromised. Innovation is unleashed by having mundane tasks taken out of the equation. An entrepreneurial team is built on excellence, confidence and passion. Changing the world comes with with chaos. Relationship is built on the abnormal. A high performing team is built on trust. Non-traditional members of a venture may not be viewed as the traditional high performers, but they are high performers by what they deliver. The same traits that make it great also tends to blow it apart. The emerging engineering and operations focus on non-traditional chemical engineering feedstocks has brought many unbeknownst to them non-traditional resources into traditional chemical engineering operations. The challenge is harnessing this new passion. There is nothing more fulfilling, exciting or satisfying.

topic: Challenges and Lessons Learned from Leading High Performing Cross Functional Teams
abstract: Cross-functional teams are significantly different from teams that are aligned on one functional level. Managing such teams with member highly accomplished in their own technical functions requires a careful leadership balance. This presentation will discuss what it takes to manage cross-functional. We will cover unique challenges and lessons learned from leading s uccessful l cross functional teams in complex corporate environments.

topic: How Can Top People be Attracted ? Some Insight
abstract: Everyone would like to claim, that the organization they lead or are a part of, is a high performance organization. In reality, not too many are. Creating and nurturing a high performance organization starts with the hiring process. But hiring is only the first step. Once staffed, the organization has to walk the talk and deliver to the employees what was promised. If leaders do not deliver on their promises, good candidates are rapidly lost. In this session we would like to discuss key elements for sustainable success: forming organizations with happy, motivated, energized and contributing collaborators.
